To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose a neural network implementation of the Sinkhorn distance that can be optimized through back propagation; and 2) we use this implementation to propose a novel unsupervised approach for cross lingual word embedding alignment that achieves state of the art performance.

(i) our unsupervised method is competitive with state-of-the-art supervised methods on the cross lingual word translation and word similarity tasks, (ii) we show that our method outperforms other unsupervised methods on the cross-lingual word translation task.

we propose a novel unsupervised cross lingual word embedding transfer method, that does not need any cross lingual supervision data, and that achieves competitive results on the benchmark datasets for bilingual dictionary induction and cross lingua word similarity prediction, over many language pairs, compared to other state-of-the-art supervised and unsupervied baselines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of unsupervised cross lingual transfer of monolingual word embeddings.
the problem of learning the cross lingual word embedding mappings without any cross lingual supervised data.
the problem of unsupervised cross lingual transfer of the word embedding spaces.

our proposed method is a very strong baseline for unsupervised cross lingual transfer of embedding spaces, especially for low resource languages.
the proposed unsupervised method is able to achieve comparable performance to supervised approaches without requiring any cross lingual supervision.
